action: Huntress advises: confirm technician clients run ScreenConnect 26.6.5 or later, disable RMM+ extension 1.0.31 and 1.0.32, review Run Command history, and check endpoints for a second ScreenConnect client. Do not connect to suspect hosts through ScreenConnect.
exec: Hundreds of managed endpoints were hit through a faulty third-party add-on; the feared spread to IT providers' own machines has not been observed.
plain: Attackers pushed fake copies of ConnectWise ScreenConnect remote-support software to hundreds of computers. Their toolkit tries to steal the login session cookie of any IT technician who connects to an infected machine, but researchers have not seen that step work.

key_findings: Huntress saw rogue ScreenConnect clients pushed to at least 288 hosts at 48 organisations on November 11 and 205 hosts at 41 organisations in a second wave on November 13.
Operators used the Run Command feature on cloud-hosted ScreenConnect panels to run commands as SYSTEM; one panel alone reached 190 downstream clients.
Entry appears tied to the third-party RMM+ extension, versions 1.0.31 and 1.0.32, which accepted a blank access key; ConnectWise disabled five extensions across about 400 partner environments.

SCKit is 16 scripts and config files that install a rogue client, hijack the real client's connection and try to steal the technician's .aspxauth session cookie (and browser cookie stores) to replay against the panel. Huntress describes CVE-2026-84869 (client flaw before 26.6.5) as background, not as the method SCKit uses.
Huntress has not seen the jump from an infected endpoint to a technician workstation succeed in any recovered log.
recommendations: Verify every technician client runs ScreenConnect 26.6.5 or later and disable the affected RMM+ extension versions.
Review Run Command and Toolbox history for unexpected mass activity and check endpoints for a second, unauthorised ScreenConnect client.
Do not connect to a suspected host through ScreenConnect; use WinRM or another out-of-band tool and isolate it until cleaned.
Remove the rogue client service, the TrapWatch scheduled task and the RelayTrap folder, then rotate ScreenConnect credentials and end web sessions from a clean device.

summary: Huntress reports two waves of attacks, on November 11 and November 13, using ScreenConnect's Run Command feature to install rogue clients on at least 288 and then 205 hosts, apparently via a flawed third-party RMM+ extension. SCKit tries to steal a technician's session cookie; Huntress has not seen that succeed. Rapid7 lists CVE-2026-127063 for RMM+'s default static API secret, not affecting ScreenConnect itself; CVE-2026-84869 is named only as background.
title: Huntress: rogue ScreenConnect clients pushed to hundreds of hosts in SCKit attacks; ConnectWise disables extensions

validation.note: Reviewed against the original Huntress report and BleepingComputer. On 22 November the Rapid7 database entry for CVE-2026-127063 (RMM+ static default API secret, published 12 November) and Cybersecurity Dive's 12 November report quoting ConnectWise were read. ConnectWise's advisories page, read 18 November, had no notice on these attacks.

date_note: Two waves, November 11 and November 13; date is the latest wave. Huntress report published November 11.

review.note: Compared 288/48 and 205/41 hosts, dates, RMM+ 1.0.31/1.0.32, 26.6.5, no technician jump observed against Huntress and BleepingComputer; 400+ partner environments was about 400 in sources, now about 400

evidence.quote: At least 288 hosts across 48 organizations that use Huntress have been affected.
This latest wave of activity has impacted 205 hosts across 41 organizations.
On November 13 at 16:12 UTC, Huntress saw another spike in detections related to SCKit.
In a precautionary measure, ConnectWise has disabled access to RMM+ extensions at about 400 environments.
The third-party RMM+ extension for ConnectWise ScreenConnect uses a static API secret by default.
